setup_common:
set -euo pipefail
git init -q --bare -b main origin.git
git init -q -b main app
cd app
git config user.name "Test Owner"
git config user.email owner@example.com
printf 'import sys


def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}."


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(greet(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "world"))
' > greet.py
printf 'import unittest

from greet import greet


class GreetTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_greets_by_name(self):
        self.assertEqual(greet("Ann"), "Hello, Ann.")
' > test_greet.py
printf 'test:
	python3 -m unittest -q
' > Makefile
printf '__pycache__/
' > .gitignore
printf 'Load the `git` skill before working in a git repository.
' > AGENTS.md
git add -A
git commit -qm "feat: greet by name"
git remote add origin ../origin.git
git push -qu origin main

evals.name: feature-goes-in-new-worktree
evals.prompt: Add a --shout option to greet.py that prints the greeting in upper case.
evals.baseline_prompt: Add a --shout option to greet.py that prints the greeting in upper case.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads the git skill, makes a new worktree on a topic branch, implements --shout there, commits it, and leaves main untouched with no pull request.
expectations: the git skill was loaded before the first file edit
main still points at the starting commit
no pull request was opened or merged
exactly one extra worktree exists, on a branch other than main
the feature is committed on that branch
the commit message follows Conventional Commits with no trailers

evals.name: feedback-goes-in-the-branch-worktree
evals.prompt: Review feedback on the --shout change in feat/shout: with --shout the greeting should end with an exclamation mark instead of a period.
evals.baseline_prompt: Review feedback on the --shout change in feat/shout: with --shout the greeting should end with an exclamation mark instead of a period.
evals.setup:
git worktree add -q -b feat/shout ../app.feat-shout main
cd ../app.feat-shout
printf 'import sys


def greet(name, shout=False):
    text = f"Hello, {name}."
    return text.upper() if shout else text


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != "--shout"]
    print(greet(args[0] if args else "world", "--shout" in sys.argv))
' > greet.py
printf '
    def test_shouts(self):
        self.assertEqual(greet("Ann", shout=True), "HELLO, ANN.")
' >> test_greet.py
git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: add --shout" && cd ../app
git config branch.feat/shout.base origin/main
git config branch.feat/shout.baseTip "$(git rev-parse main)"
evals.expected_output: The agent makes the change in the existing feat/shout worktree, commits it there, creates no new branch or worktree, and leaves main untouched.
expectations: main still points at the starting commit
no pull request was opened or merged
no new branch or worktree was created
checks: [ "$(git worktree list | wc -l)" -eq 2 ] && [ "$(git for-each-ref refs/heads | wc -l)" -eq 2 ]

evals.prompt: Add a --shout option to greet.py that prints the greeting in upper case.
evals.baseline_prompt: Add a --shout option to greet.py that prints the greeting in upper case.
evals.expected_output: With webdavis.policy off the agent does not apply the owner's rules: no worktree is made, the change happens in the current checkout.
